papers.title: Orthogonal Symmetric Nonnegative Matrix Factorization With Low-Rank Tensor Representation for Multilayer Network Community Detection
papers.abstract: Multilayer networks community detection plays an important role in data mining. It can discover the latent representations of network structures for effectively completing downstream tasks. However, existing community detection methods rarely consider the relationships between multilayer networks. In addition, the noise contained in the networks always leads to the degradation of detection performance. To address the above issues, this article proposes an orthogonal symmetric nonnegative matrix factorization (SNMF) with low-rank tensor representation (OSNMFTR) for multilayer networks community detection. Specifically, the proposed approach obtains the latent representation of each network via orthogonal SNMF, then a clean self-representation tensor is got based on subspace learning. Finally, to discover the high-order relationships among each network, a weighted tensor nuclear norm is utilized to constrain the tensor to make it low-rank. An algorithm based on the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMMs) is designed to solve the OSNMFTR model. The experiments on nine datasets show the superior performance of the proposed approach.

papers.title: Self-Supervised Graph Convolutional with Locality Preserving Low-Pass Embedding for Large-Scale Hyperspectral Image Clustering
papers.abstract: Hyperspectral images (HSI) captured via remote sensing systems contain numerous consecutive narrow spectral bands, offering rich spatial-spectral data across the electromagnetic spectrum. Given their distinct benefits, HSI has gained significant interest and found broad utilization in domains like military surveillance, urban planning, biochemical analysis, wildfire monitoring, and object identification.

papers.title: Introduction to Image and Video Coding
papers.abstract: This chapter provides an introductory overview of image and video coding. We explore the transition from continuous real-world scenes to discrete digital images, and present the basic knowledge of image and video signal processing. Color images can be decomposed into RGB components, illustrating how they contribute to the color intensity. The YUV video data format is also discussed, as well as its advantages over RGB for transmitting image and video signals. There are various YUV sampling techniques, such as 4:4:4, 4:2:2, and 4:2:0, in order to balance the visual quality fidelity and the data storage efficiency. In the realm of AI-based image and video coding, the importance of diverse and high quality datasets for training and evaluating compression algorithms is undoubted. There are several typical image and video datasets, with unique characteristics and applications in compression. Lastly, the necessity of compression is analyzed in modern digital ecosystems, advocating for AI-driven compression techniques that surpass traditional methods in achieving higher rate distortion performance. The quality assessment for compressed image and video data should include both the sides ofsubjective and objective assessments.

papers.title: Deep Learning-based Image Coding
papers.abstract: The development of computer vision has led to the successful application of deep learning to image compression.. Unlike the conventional coding framework, learned image compression (LIC) methods are built upon neural networks and optimized end-to-end with a unified loss function instead of individually tuning each module. In this way, LIC methods can achieve global optimization, have demonstrated outstanding rate-distortion (RD) performance, and exceed conventional codecs such as JPEG and BPG. This chapter provides a systematic study of LIC, which can be categorized into three types based on functionality: lossless image compression, lossy image compression, and generative image compression. Specifically, lossy image compression as a crucial technique is reviewed at both the framework and component levels. Numerous works are proposed to enhance lossy learned image compression in terms of transformation and entropy models, which will be thoroughly discussed in the core components subsection. Following that, generative image compression, mainly for human perception, is reviewed as well. It can maintain the subjective perception at extremely low bit rates.

papers.title: Implementations for AI-based Image and Video Coding
papers.abstract: This chapter will delve into the growing challenge of deploying complex neural networks in resource-constrained environments, particularly within the realm of image and video coding. As neural networks become more sophisticated, their demand for computational resources escalates, complicating their application in edge and mobile devices. To address this, lightweight techniques like pruning, quantization, and knowledge distillation are used to decrease model size and computation complexity without sacrificing performance. By streamlining neural networks, these methods facilitate more efficient deployments and enhance real-time processing capabilities. This chapter will focus on various lightweight approaches and hardware implementations specifically designed for learning-based image and video compression networks.

papers.title: Deep Learning-based Video Coding
papers.abstract: Video coding is essential for efficient storage, transmission, and playback of video content across digital platforms. Numerous techniques have been developed to balance file size reduction with the preservation of perceptual video quality. Traditional standards like H.264 and H.265 have dominated the field, employing methods such as motion estimation and discrete cosine transform (DCT). However, these approaches face challenges in achieving significant compression gains while maintaining high visual quality, particularly at low bit rates. The introduction of deep learning has revolutionized video coding by leveraging neural networks to exploit spatial and temporal correlations within video frames, resulting in improved compression efficiency and quality. Early developments in deep learning-based video compression began in the 2010s, aided by advancements in GPUs and large datasets. This field has rapidly evolved, with various techniques emerging, including convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and recurrent neural networks (RNNs). These deep learning methods can be categorized based on techniques like intra-frame or inter-frame coding, architecture selections, and the degree of end-to-end compression. Overall, the integration of deep learning into video compression has led to significant advancements, enhancing video storage, transmission, and streaming without sacrificing quality. The following sections will explore specific techniques and innovations in this domain.

papers.title: Quality Assessment and Perception Models for Image and Video
papers.abstract: This chapter provides a comprehensive overview of quality assessment and perception models for images and videos, focusing on key concepts such as subjective and objective quality assessment frameworks, Just-Noticeable-Distortion (JND), Salient Object Detection (SOD). Subjective and objective quality assessment methods are examined, with subjective approaches like Mean Opinion Score (MOS) serving as benchmarks, while objective methods—Full-Reference (FR), Reduced-Reference (RR), and No-Reference (NR)—leverage metrics such as PSNR and SSIM, alongside deep learning models for enhanced performance. JND is introduced as a critical perceptual threshold in the human visual system (HVS), distinguishing perceptible distortions from imperceptible ones to optimize quality assessment models. The discussion on SOD covers both image and video domains. This chapter also reviews JND datasets and models in pixel and frequency domains, emphasizing their applications in image/video coding and quality assessment. By integrating perceptual models with advanced computational techniques, this chapter underscores the importance of aligning quality assessment with human visual perception for multimedia applications.

papers.title: Open Source Projects for AI-based Image and Video Coding
papers.abstract: Open source projects play a pivotal role in advancing AI-based image and video coding technologies by fostering collaborations, sharing knowledge, and inspiring innovations. This chapter introduces several prominent open source projects that are shaping the landscape of AI-based image and video compression. It begins by highlighting the significance of open source contributions in driving accessibility, inclusivity, and efficiency in AI research. The chapter provides an overview of key projects, including CompressAI, a library offering tools for end-to-end image and video compression, and OpenVVC, a real-time software decoder aligned with the H.266/VVC standard. The chapter then delves into two novel open source projects developed for deep learning-based compression, including OpenDIC and OpenDMC. OpenDIC focuses on single-frame image compression using state-of-the-art algorithms implemented in frameworks like MindSpore and PyTorch, while OpenDMC extends these principles to multi-frame video compression. Both projects offer comprehensive algorithm repositories to facilitate further research and development.

papers.title: Compression Artifacts Removal for Image and Video Coding
papers.abstract: Image and video lossy compression algorithms ease the storage and transmission of information under limited bandwidth. However, lossy compression modes inevitably cause a decrease in signal fidelity and poor subjective experience. How to remove compression artifacts in a post-processing manner at the decoding end has become one of the trends in point cloud enhancement tasks. Recently, numerous of compression artifact removal methods with deep learning have shown excellent performance and generalization. On the one hand, these methods have widely migrated general quality enhancement methods from images to videos. On the other hand, with the continuous development of the characteristics of compression distortion and feature extraction paradigms, deep learning-based compression artifact removal methods will show better performance in the future.

papers.title: Deep Learning-based 3D and Multimodal Coding
papers.abstract: 3D image compression is a special compression technology for 3D image data, which aims to reduce the volume of image files and maintain the highest image quality as possible. Unlike traditional 2D image compression, 3D image compression requires consideration of additional dimensions and complex data structures because 3D images contain depth information in space. In 3D image compression, a number of special algorithms and techniques are often used to effectively reduce the amount of data while preserving important details and structure as much as possible. This helps reduce costs in terms of storage and transmission and improves the efficiency and performance of images in a variety of applications. Within this chapter, the emphasis shifts towards methods for deep learning-based 3D and multimodal image compression methods.
